[mv-k06-v751] Therefore, through the dissolution of past and future, and also through the dissolution of the present, this god, the lord of consciousness himself, fully makes time manifest.

[mv-k06-v752] Thus, for this consciousness whose nature is to manifest time, transmigration—containing the manifestation of its own nature—appears among beings as consisting of being and nonbeing within its own form.

[mv-k06-v753] Abiding in its own form is called the unfolding of knowerhood: 'this is not what I am', and 'I am what is not this', and also 'this is that'.

[mv-k06-v754] The varied cognition expressed as 'this is not this' is the supreme appearing of nonbeing; but in that pure knowerhood there is no separate abiding of such distinctions.

[mv-k06-v755] In that isolated aspect there is no cognition at all, so what use is that isolated state? But every worldly state of being a knower is of this differentiated kind.

[mv-k06-v756] There, nonbeing becomes an object of cognition, and that happens through the grace of time; for this perfectly full reality bears the form of all things and the self of all.

[mv-k06-v757] Where could the knower stand, where cognition, and where the known object? For if knower and the rest were absolutely real, their status could not be merely relative.

[mv-k06-v758] The being of the knower and the rest is conceived only from the known; whether their mutual form is absent or present, it cannot stand independently because of their incompatibility.

[mv-k06-v759] This view fails because it would lead to overextension everywhere, would entail omniscience and the like, and because noncontributing factors do not manifest all at once.

[mv-k06-v760] If knowerhood were produced by some other known object, then its own arising would depend on something else again, and so it would remain as if unarisen.

[mv-k06-v761] Therefore this full consciousness, Shiva, dividing its own aspect, constructs the differentiated part beginning with 'not I' and also the object 'this'.

[mv-k06-v762] The 'I' takes to itself, to that extent, the fullness of everything other; and from what is other there also arises the withdrawing sense of 'not I'.

[mv-k06-v763] These two parts mutually exclude each other; the own 'I' conceals the 'this' part, which stands in cognition, within its own 'I'-aspect.

[mv-k06-v764] It remains and does not dissolve it, just like a pot covered by a cloth; that same thing, though tied by convention, remains established in cognition.

[mv-k06-v765] The 'this' arises from inner contraction that excludes the 'I'-part, and the 'I' arises from within through exclusion of the whole mass of 'thisness'.

[mv-k06-v766] From the exclusion of one's own 'I' and the exclusion of other and other 'I'-senses there arises manifestation; relying on which, the six deities of empty form proceed.

[mv-k07-v901] The boundless manifold of difference, treated in brief and in full, is set forth; and now, in due order, comes the reckoning of its divisions from water onward, from root to end.

[mv-k09-v1201] Surely, when their gross form is suddenly burned away, things forcibly attain unity with the great blazing light of awareness by their very nature; this is regarded as the supreme offering in the Bhairava tradition.

[mv-k09-v1202] When entities are properly offered by method into the fire within one's own awareness, they abandon the division of difference and, by their own power, kindle that very fire.

[mv-k09-v1203] Whatever sense-object consciousness creates before itself by its own will and by the force of its creative nature becomes fit for meditation on that very object.

[mv-k09-v1204] For although the abode of consciousness is formless and yet made of all forms, for those who seek results some particular form is established as the object of meditation.

[mv-k09-v1205] Just as, even within a nondual and full reality, someone fetching water eagerly seeks a pot by setting aside other forms, so too a particular form may be chosen.

[mv-k09-v1206] In the same way, through the unfolding of the supreme Lord's self-restriction, some particular form gives rise to some particular conception of a result.

[mv-k09-v1207] But for one whose activity is the fullness of consciousness and who desires no result at all, meditation in the form of the whole universe unfolds at all times.

[mv-k09-v1208] For the Kula yogin reeling from the intoxicant of the surging Bhairava essence, whatever arises, in whatever way it arises, simply arises.

[mv-k09-v1209] The bodily absorption whose nature is delight and melting is, in the unsurpassed teaching, the seal that has taken the whole world as its seal.

[mv-k09-v1210] This rare method of yoga abides in the heart of someone whose wheel of consciousness becomes clear, quickly, as in the case of one who is in his final birth.

[mv-k09-v1211] Even while being seen by people and remaining in the condition of bodily bondage, when yoga has matured he attains in an instant an incomparable awareness.

[mv-k09-v1212] But right here, the intellect of our earlier teachers strongly affirmed the non-presence of the delusions of worldly experience.

[mv-k09-v1213] Enough with the Vedic, Samkhya, dualist, logical, Buddhist, and worldly views, and with Pancaratra, ritual scriptures, Siddhanta, and the rest.

[mv-k09-v1214] All those various practitioners, cultivating the fitting portions of knowledge and action and established in their own procedures, act according to what is appropriate for them.

[mv-k09-v1215] Where the very extensive sequence of acts such as sowing, implanting, and digging was carried out by the many branches of the Shambhava teaching.

[mv-k09-v1216] The unsurpassed fruit of that tree of consciousness-Bhairava is this, beyond practices such as life-stage observances and even ascetic marks like matted hair and ointments.

[mv-k09-v1217] Where no difference is found between what is done and what is not done, for those who rest in that very yoga the pageantry of worldly existence dissolves.

[mv-k09-v1218] Like a mass of snow in the great summer, it melts away by itself; for when this juicy nectar of awareness is savored, that is enough.

[mv-k09-v1219] Great raptures flow forth, of which there is no number; their manifestations were already set out at length before, but here in Abhinavagupta's treatment only some are definitively stated.

[mv-k09-v1220] In the rich fragrance of the ketaki flower, the bee alone is the connoisseur, not the fly; likewise, in the worship of the supreme nondual Bhairava, some rare one delights, not one deluded by duality.

[mv-k09-v1221] For one established here, no purification of any kind would need to be done anywhere; for what in the world, whose very nature is Bhairava, could be impure?

[mv-k09-v1222] And even if the mass of beings were impure, by what means could purification be effected? In that way there would be infinite regress and likewise a futile mutual dependence.

[mv-k09-v1223] When the impure is concealed, what is called the pure dissolves as well; for that is constituted by its opposite and is not established by its own nature, like blue.

[mv-k09-v1224] Therefore there is no insistence at all on either grasping or rejecting sense objects; for one whose nature is the consciousness of supreme Bhairava, enjoyership surges forth by itself.

[mv-k09-v1225] Since everything established here fits together by this path, the whole system is coherent. If one rejects this path, surely no other approach attains any coherence at all.

[mv-k09-v1226] For example, initiation is that which cuts away impurities; but how can this possibly be explained in the view of those who assert difference?

[mv-k09-v1227] For how can the so-called impurity cover a self whose nature is consciousness? And where is there any act of covering for an all-pervading being?

[mv-k09-v1228] Light is never covered by darkness, because the very arising of light is an act that destroys darkness.

[mv-k09-v1229] Moreover, covering is said to be an obstruction of something that moves, like rays; so how could that apply to an all-pervading being that has no motion?

[mv-k09-v1230] Or else, covering is merely the concealment of knowability, as when a pot is covered by a cloth; it is not an alteration of its own nature.

[mv-k09-v1231] But selves, because they are of the nature of consciousness, do not admit knowability; so to speak of their being covered is not fitting even in words.

[mv-k09-v1232] But surely, one objects, those atomic selves are knowable to the Lord. How so? For what is of the nature of consciousness is not knowable, since that would conceal its conscious nature.

[mv-k09-v1233] The expression 'awareness is knowable' seems to recall its own fellow, the statement 'my mother is barren,' since both are self-contradictory.

[mv-k09-v1234] Moreover, the Lord's omniscience would be impaired to that extent, because he would not know the covered atomic selves; yet there would be no harm to the selves themselves.

[mv-k09-v1235] But surely, when a blue object is uncovered the knower sees it, and when it is covered there is no seeing; likewise, one might say, an omniscient being covered by impurity would be obstructed.

[mv-k09-v1236] Not so. In that case, a cloth obstructs the outgoing rays of sight, but there is no possibility of covering the knower himself.

[mv-k09-v1237] It is clear that a non-pervading impurity cannot be the coverer of what is all-pervading; even in a pot, it would by its own nature make space non-empty only in a limited way.

[mv-k09-v1238] And if impurity produces no effect because the self is not subject to modification, how can it be capable of covering? Surely, sir, what then?

[mv-k09-v1239] Indeed, its covering is said to be merely the existence of impurity; the atomic self is described as covered simply because it has impurity as a second.

[mv-k09-v1240] Alas, by this reasoning, even for those of the stated nature there would truly be a covering of Shiva, merely from the existence of impurity.

[mv-k09-v1241] Moreover, if the self covered by impurity does not even know the impurity, then in that non-awareness of it, is another impurity to be posited?

[mv-k09-v1242] But what of it? Let it know the impurity. Then, without vidya and kala, there would be omniscience; and if the impurity were known, the self could abandon it by various contrived means.

[mv-k09-v1243] Let the self abandon it by those various contrived means; and if so, what covering would that impurity produce in the self?

[mv-k09-v1244] How would this self come to be a knower and doer with respect to pots and such things? Surely, one replies, because vidya and kala are held to be the basis of limited knowing and doing.

[mv-k09-v1245] In this way the deluded are deceived, but not the wise: this maya is inert by nature, and kala and the rest are its offspring.

[mv-k09-v1246] How could what is non-conscious be capable of manifesting consciousness? And if all-pervading consciousness were manifested, how could it be qualified by limitedness and such attributes?

[mv-k09-v1247] How could it become qualified? For that is fitting only for things that have parts. But surely, one objects, God, using kala and vidya, could manifest consciousness.

[mv-k09-v1248] Let him manifest it in all ways—alas, there is no incapacity in him. But if there is insistence on an eternal impurity, how will liberation ever come about?

[mv-k09-v1249] The claim that impurity has an obstructing power which sometimes stops and sometimes acts is foolish talk.

[mv-k09-v1250] Insentient things cannot deliberate, so how could that selective operation happen? If so, one must admit that God is the cause even in that case.

[mv-k09-v1251] For what reason would that God set that power in motion, or for what reason would he make it stop again once it has been set in motion?

[mv-k09-v1252] If the answer is that God acts from autonomy, then let that plenitude alone be accepted. Why bring in impurity, which is of the nature of darkness, and why suppose any maturation of it at all?

[mv-k09-v1253] For maturation, by involving a connection with another state, would destroy mala's fixed nature. By this reasoning, the idea that a soul is impelled by God's will because of its connection with impurity is refuted.

[mv-k09-v1254] The claim that the bound soul, caught up in the desire for enjoyment, is favored by creation is struck at the root; that consequence follows from what has been shown.

[mv-k09-v1255] They know impurity to be nothing but the mere play of concealing one's own self. For why would the autonomous, all-pervading Lord not manifest anything within himself?

[mv-k09-v1256] And as for karma, which is also accepted, let that first be examined. For even if the connection with karma remains, how can there be such a state as the great dissolution?

[mv-k09-v1257] How can there be a great dissolution, or a great creation? Surely, one may say, karma becomes restrained there by the will of God.

[mv-k09-v1258] Does the Lord do this through karma's inactivity, or by depending on another karma, or not? In the first alternative, that very possibility becomes an issue.

[mv-k09-v1259] If that is impossible, in what respect could he possess sovereignty? Then all this—creation, dissolution, and the rest—would come about from karma alone.

[mv-k09-v1260] But if, without depending on karma, he restrains karmas, then let the all-pervading Lord keep them restrained always.

[mv-k09-v1261] But surely their nature is to produce enjoyment. How could that be an intrinsic nature if it has come to depend on another condition?

[mv-k09-v1262] For the intrinsic nature of things is independent. Therefore, whatever form karmas have when they do not depend on the Lord's direction—that is their own true nature.

[mv-k09-v1263] And do the karmas dissolved in the great dissolution, or even those that still persist, get awakened by God? What, indeed, is accomplished by those karmas?

[mv-k09-v1264] If it is said to be for the maturation of impurity, that too has been thoroughly dismissed. And this self is all-pervading—what, indeed, can karma do to it?

[mv-k09-v1265] This examination has already been elaborated at length. In the clay, stick, wheel, and threads, it is the intelligent Lord who stands as the true agent.

[mv-k09-v1266] In what respect, indeed, does the potter's agency stand, especially in the sprouting and growth of seeds that have not been ploughed or cultivated?

[mv-k09-v1267] Let it be a cause earlier, but not in the crops—what principle is that? This is a bad deed and that a good deed, distinguished by the difference in their fruits.

[mv-k09-v1268] If that division is made, does only his will unfold there? If he is autonomous, why would he adopt a will of his own that causes harm to others?

[mv-k09-v1269] Why would he, who is always filled with compassion, adopt such a will? But surely, one may say, karma is such by its own nature and therefore gives those fruits.

[mv-k09-v1274] Thus, from the standpoint of duality, this so-called karma is not well-reasoned. Here only a brief summary is given, while the fuller elaboration has been shown elsewhere.

[mv-k09-v1275] The Lord is one, whose very nature is consciousness; therefore he is indeed the all-doer by his own nature. Because of diversity, he is spoken of as connected with karma.

[mv-k09-v1276] And that so-called Maya, which is established as the cause of the universe, containing within her womb the elements of the tattvas ending with earth—if she is clearly eternal...

[mv-k09-v1281] What part would not be known, even where dependence on manifestation is assumed? In the view of the satkarya theorists, the universe is clearly established even in the cause.

[mv-k09-v1282] Thus, for the universe to be clearly present in Maya would be incongruous, since Siva and the selves are pervasive, together with the tattvas and mutually so.

[mv-k09-v1283] And how indeed could they exist, given the concealment of pervasiveness? The supreme expansion of consciousness is its pervasion, and in division it is spoken of accordingly.

[mv-k09-v1284] The group of coverings born of Maya, as well as the collection of instruments, has already been examined before, and the group of effects has also been discussed.

[mv-k09-v1285] As long as the universe, devoid of resting on the state of Siva, does not shine forth, this is merely talk of its autonomy; let that be understood.

[mv-k09-v1286] Thus, in the absence of impurity and the like, what initiation could there be, who would be the initiator, and who the recipient? None of this fits.

[mv-k09-v1287] How could the installation of the entire path in the disciple, the path, the fire, the vessel, the mandala, the ladle, the hand, and so on, be possible?

[mv-k09-v1288] Surely they would not all be present in that way. But, one may object, by the power of conception this entire relation of purifier and purified has indeed been declared.

[mv-k09-v1289] If what is merely imagined could bear fruit, then truly those who have gained riches in the kingdom of fantasy would triumph by attaining the repose of heavenly sovereignty.

[mv-k09-v1290] Do states that follow the path of strong, vivid conception not bear fruit in that way, like the destruction of poison through meditation and the like?

[mv-k09-v1291] Meditation is precisely firmness of conception; but meditation tainted by doubt does not bear fruit at all, because it grasps two alternatives.

[mv-k09-v1292] Look—if its fruit were to arise from the application of conception, why would you desire some external entities that are not made of consciousness?

[mv-k09-v1293] By conception alone there is consecration pertaining to the pit, fire, guru, and disciple; and that same thing, appearing as the fruit, remains as that consciousness.

[mv-k09-v1294] And the manifestation in such a form of autonomous consciousness should indeed be understood as initiation, by which beings are liberated.

[mv-k09-v1295] For that very reason, no sequence or fixed rule has been determined here in the scripture regarding the essential nature, taking, or measure of sesame, ghee, and the like.

[mv-k09-v1296] But surely, what fixed rule is there in mantras? For the supreme form is declared to partake of all letters; so how could initiation not be the same way?

[mv-k09-v1297] Thus, the burning of letters as you approve it is indeed beneficial; but for those who have not yet attained firm establishment, a definite rule certainly applies to them.

[mv-k09-v1298] This mantric rule has been declared and it serves a real purpose, for those mantras are awakened and move along the path of reflective awareness.

[mv-k09-v1299] Because the light of consciousness is autonomous, the mantras, made of agency, enter that very teacher through the application of identity with it.

[mv-k09-v1300] They make him autonomous, and even instruments attain agency; thus, initiation and whatever other rites are accepted become possible.

[mv-k09-v1301] What, indeed, is to be done by those who act, and how could there even be prohibition? Both are established right here, for all of that is enjoined here.

[mv-k09-v1302] And all this is prohibited only from that other standpoint; for when its prohibition is clearly shown, what force does it have for one who rests on the nondual path?

[mv-k09-v1303] Even prohibition is enjoined, and that too is prohibited; thus the ocean of one's own awareness surges abundantly within itself.

[mv-k09-v1304] Thus this entire universe is beautiful with the bliss of the world, and in this way it utterly dissolves the opposing element of difference.

[mv-k09-v1305] From the moon of knowledge risen from the mouth of the Supreme Lord, beautiful rays radiant with the fullness of their own light spread in all directions.

[mv-k09-v1306] The deadly poison that darkens the moon of all beings, melted by the mere touch of the mass of rays from Shiva's moon, turns into an elixir.

[mv-k09-v1307] Plunging there unceasingly and reeling from drinking that essence, we become that essence itself and abide pure, freed from the three kinds of suffering.

[mv-k09-v1308] The mouth of the Supreme Lord is said to be his power, namely will; having arisen, that will takes on the functioning of the moon of knowledge in the distinct states beginning with Īśvara.

[mv-k09-v1309] The fully spread mass of rays streaming forth on all sides from that moon is indeed the Supreme Lord's own power, declared to consist of action and to be made of the world.

[mv-k09-v1310] Thus this, full of the three powers, expands as the supreme Bhairava alone; nothing different from it could exist, and its own expansion is proclaimed as its victory.

[mv-k09-v1311] From that very reality these powers clearly conquer the world; the meaning becomes manifest and fits for us, since such a connection with many expressions belongs to that fullness and accommodates the division of statements.

[mv-k10-v1351] The fruit may be clear and primary, or it may be the final result; it may belong to the main element or to an auxiliary; and it may appear in its opposite, in another side, or in some other opposing condition.
